headline: Biman Bangladesh Airlines signs deal to buy 10 aircraft from Airbus
summary: The fleet expansion includes four wide-body A350-900s and six narrow-body A321neo jets to modernize the national carrier's operations.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has signed a formal agreement with Airbus to purchase 10 new aircraft, aiming to expand and modernize its current fleet.
The deal includes four wide-body A350-900 aircraft and six narrow-body A321neo jets. The signing ceremony, titled 'Spreading Our Wings Together', took place at a hotel in Dhaka.
The A350-900 models are reported to be 25 percent more fuel-efficient and emit less carbon. Depending on the configuration, they can accommodate between 332 and 480 passengers.
The A350-900 also features a long-range capability of approximately 18,000km on a single flight, making it suitable for long-haul routes.
The A321neo series aircraft are designed for medium passenger capacities, with a range of up to 7,500km and a seating capacity ranging from 180 to 244 passengers.
The ceremony was attended by Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, Biman Chairman Rumi A Hossain, and Airbus India and South Asia President Jürgen Westermeier.
caption:

The A350-900 also features a long-range capability of approximately 18,000km on a single flight, making it suitable for long-haul routes.

The A321neo series aircraft are designed for medium passenger capacities, with a range of up to 7,500km and a seating capacity ranging from 180 to 244 passengers.

The ceremony was attended by Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, Biman Chairman Rumi A Hossain, and Airbus India and South Asia President Jürgen Westermeier.

headline_marked: German tourist [[loses bag with laptop and camera]] at Natore railway station
headline: German tourist loses bag with laptop and camera at Natore railway station
summary: The tourist accidentally got off at the wrong station and left his belongings with a railway official who then disappeared with the items.
details: A German tourist visiting Bangladesh has lost his laptop and camera after leaving them with a railway official at Natore railway station.
The incident occurred when the tourist accidentally disembarked at the wrong station.
He entrusted his bag containing the expensive electronics to a railway official for safekeeping while he sorted out his journey.
However, the official allegedly disappeared with the bag and its contents.
The tourist has sought help from local authorities to recover his belongings.
Local police and railway police are now investigating the case to identify and locate the missing official.
caption:
